title: Using cryoEM and cryoET to visualize membrane penetration of a non-enveloped virus
author: Xia, Zhou
materials: Ultrathin carbon on Lacey Carbon support film

steps.title: Thaw BHK-21 cells
steps.instruction: Place the cryopreserved BHK-21 vial in a 35 °C water bath and agitate gently until ice melts (≤ 2 min).

steps.title: Transfer cells to T75 flask
steps.instruction: Decontaminate the vial with 70 % ethanol, add the cells to a T75 flask inside a biosafety cabinet and slowly add 14 mL DMEM supplemented with 10 % FBS, penicillin 100 U/mL and streptomycin 100 µg/mL.

steps.title: Incubate and monitor attachment
steps.instruction: Gently shake the flask to separate cells, then place it in a 35 °C incubator with 5 % CO₂. After 4–6 h examine under an inverted microscope; if most cells are attached, replace the medium with 15 mL fresh DMEM (same supplements).

steps.title: Grow cells to confluence
steps.instruction: Keep the flask in the incubator for 2 days until cells reach ~90 % confluence.

steps.title: Rinse and trypsinize cells
steps.instruction: Discard the medium, rinse gently with 10 mL PBS to remove serum, discard PBS, then add 3 mL trypsin‑EDTA solution. Return the flask to the incubator and monitor; detachment usually occurs within 5–10 min (slow at 25 °C or dilute trypsin if digestion is too fast).

steps.title: Stop trypsin digestion
steps.instruction: Add 7 mL fresh DMEM to neutralize trypsin and pipette gently to disperse the cells.

steps.title: Subculture into T175 flasks
steps.instruction: Transfer 2 mL of the cell suspension (1:5 subcultivation) and add 33 mL fresh medium to each new T175 flask (recommended subculture ratio 1:3–1:10).

steps.title: Scale up to ten T175 flasks
steps.instruction: Repeat the growth (steps 4–7) until you have 10 T175 flasks each at ~90 % confluence.

steps.title: Replace medium before infection
steps.instruction: In each of the 10 confluent T175 flasks, discard old medium and add 35 mL fresh DMEM containing 10 % FBS, penicillin 100 U/mL and streptomycin 100 µg/mL.

steps.title: Inoculate flasks with BTV stock
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL of BTV stock to each flask and shake gently to mix. (Typical stock titer ≈ 1.5 × 10⁵ PFU/mL; use ~0.03 MOI.)

steps.title: Incubate infected cultures
steps.instruction: Place flasks in the incubator for ~70 h, checking at 48 h; when ~80 % of cells are rounded (≈ 70 h), proceed to harvest.

steps.title: Harvest cells and lyse
steps.instruction: Discard the media, add 1.5 mL pre‑chilled lysis buffer to each flask, scrape cells, combine all cells into a 50 mL tube and bring total volume to 20 mL with lysis buffer. Pipette up/down several times and keep on ice for 15 min.

steps.title: Clarify lysate and sucrose cushion
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 2 000 × g for 10 min to pellet nuclei. Prepare a double cushion in a tube: 4 mL 66 % (w/w) sucrose at the bottom and 10 mL 50 % (w/v) sucrose on top. Load the supernatant onto the cushion.

steps.title: Ultracentrifuge and collect virus band
steps.instruction: Spin the tube in an SW28 rotor at 100 000 × g for 1 h at 4 °C. Using a flashlight, locate the virus band at the interface, carefully remove the upper layer and collect the band (< 1 mL) with a 1 mL pipette. Dilute the collected volume 10‑fold with 20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.8 to a final volume of 10 mL. (If > 1 mL is collected, dilute to 20 mL and split into two tubes for the next step.)

steps.title: Detergent treatment and clarification
steps.instruction: Add N‑Lauroylsarcosine sodium salt to a final concentration of 0.1 % (v/v), pipet several times to disperse aggregates and incubate on ice for 10 min. Then centrifuge at 16 000 × g for 10 min to clarify.

steps.title: Density gradient ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: In a new SW41 tube, add 1 mL 30 % (w/v) sucrose to the bottom, slowly layer the clarified supernatant on top, and ultracentrifuge at 80 000 × g for 1 h at 4 °C (SW41 Ti rotor).

steps.title: Resuspend purified virus
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 20 µL 20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.8. Verify integrity by negative‑stain EM; acceptable samples show > 5 particles per image.

steps.title: Prepare lipid mixture
steps.instruction: Mix DOPC, DOPE, cholesterol and LBPA in a molar ratio of 50:20:15:15. Dissolve each lipid in chloroform at 25 mg/mL (DOPC 100 µL, DOPE 40 µL, cholesterol 30 µL, LBPA 30 µL) and combine in a glass vial using glass syringes.

steps.title: Dry lipids and remove solvent
steps.instruction: Evaporate chloroform under a gentle nitrogen stream in a fume hood, then place the vial in a vacuum desiccator for 3 h to eliminate residual solvent.

steps.title: Hydrate lipids and form vesicles
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL liposome buffer to the dried lipids, pipette repeatedly, and transfer the suspension to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Freeze‑thaw and extrude liposomes
steps.instruction: Freeze‑thaw the suspension 5 times in liquid nitrogen, then extrude the sample 21 passes through a 0.2 µm polycarbonate membrane using a Mini Extruder.

steps.title: Store liposomes
steps.instruction: Keep the prepared liposomes at 4 °C and use them within one week.

steps.title: Glow‑discharge EM grids
steps.instruction: Place thin continuous carbon‑film coated lacey grids in an easiGlow device and glow‑discharge for 1 min.

steps.title: Adjust liposome pH
steps.instruction: Add sodium citrate buffer to the liposome suspension to reach a final concentration of 100 mM and pH 5.5.

steps.title: Apply virus to grid
steps.instruction: Pipette 2 µL purified BTV virion onto a glow‑discharged grid and incubate for 1 min.

steps.title: Add liposomes and blot
steps.instruction: Manually blot the grid with filter paper to remove excess virus, then add 2.5 µL of the acidified liposome suspension onto the grid.

steps.title: Plunge‑freeze grids in Vitrobot
steps.instruction: Mount the grid in a Vitrobot Mark IV, incubate for 30 s, then blot for 20 s at 8 °C with blot force 15 and 100 % humidity (pre‑saturate blot paper for 20 min). Immediately plunge‑freeze in liquid ethane.

steps.title: Prepare cryoET grids with gold beads
steps.instruction: For cryoET, mix the acidified liposomes with 10 nm gold beads before applying to the grid (otherwise follow steps 23‑27).

steps.title: Assess grid quality
steps.instruction: Examine grids on a TF20 microscope; if ice is too thick increase blot time/force, if virus concentration is low repeat purification, and if no virus‑liposome interaction is seen extend incubation in step 24. Freeze remaining virus sample under the same conditions and store grids in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Load grids into Titan Krios
steps.instruction: Insert the optimized grids into a Titan Krios equipped with a Gatan GIF Quantum LS and a Gatan K2 Summit detector; operate at 300 kV in super‑resolution mode.

steps.title: Align microscope and set SerialEM
steps.instruction: Perform careful alignment of the microscope and configure data‑collection parameters in SerialEM.

steps.title: Map grid and select squares
steps.instruction: Acquire a low‑magnification map at 135×, choose squares with appropriate ice thickness, then acquire a medium‑magnification map at 4800× for each selected square.

steps.title: Record single‑particle movies
steps.instruction: At 105 000× (0.68 Å/pixel, super‑resolution), set defocus to –1.8 to –2.6 µm, expose for 8 s divided into 40 frames, delivering a total dose of 40–50 e⁻/Å² per movie.

steps.title: Collect cryoET tilt series
steps.instruction: At 53 000× (1.276 Å/pixel, super‑resolution), record tilt series from –60° to +60° in 3° increments using a grouped dose‑symmetric scheme; acquire 8–10 frames per tilt for a cumulative dose of ~120 e⁻/Å², with defocus –3 to –4.5 µm.
